args.title: Only treat a quote as starting a quoted CSV field
args.body:
File: src/ingest/parser.ts

splitFields() toggles inQuotes on any double-quote character, even one appearing in the middle of an unquoted field (e.g. Monitor 27" Dell). Per CSV convention, a field should only be treated as quoted when the quote is the first character of the field; any other quote should be kept as a literal character. Update splitFields() to only enter quoted mode when `current === ""` at the start of a field, so inch marks and other embedded quotes in plain fields don't swallow the rest of the line.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The bug is in splitFields(): it toggles quoted mode on any double-quote character, even one in the middle of an unquoted field like `Monitor 27" Dell U2724D`, so the rest of the line gets swallowed as one field. The fix should only enter quoted mode when the quote is the first character of a field (i.e. `current === ""`), leaving other quotes as literal characters. I've opened a draft PR with this approach rather than merging #952 as-is, since treating every quote as literal everywhere could break genuinely CSV-quoted fields that contain commas; that PR wasn't reviewed here.
